text: How should the CTO explain risk in autonomous operational decisioning?
claudePromptBoundary: Full production prompt is reconstructed from current source template and captured source packet. ai_egress_audit stores prompt hash/snapshot refs, not raw prompt text by default.
claudeResponse:
" That reframes the board conversation from AI capability to operational accountability, which is the register a CTO can actually defend.
The specific risks I would name, grounded in the loaded IROPS context: model-decision risk on crew legality, PNR reaccommodation, and turn sequencing where a bad autonomous action creates DOT exposure or crew-contract breach; data-freshness risk across the crew legality feed, flight status, PNR events, and operational event store, where stale inputs drive confidently wrong decisions; control-evidence risk, meaning no signed model-risk tier, no override log, no accountable control owner tied to each AI initiative; and vendor/platform risk on the OCC platform, Crew Recovery Optimizer, and PSS mainframe gateway, where SLA and integration dependencies aren't yet contractually linked to the autonomous decision path.
The honest posture: fund readiness before autonomous scale, and keep customer- or crew-impacting actions human-in-loop until model risk and data certification sign off.
Risk table for the board conversation: | Risk | Control / mitigation | Owner | Severity | Evidence / gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Autonomous action violates crew legality or DOT customer-care obligation | Model-risk tiering + HITL gate for crew and passenger-facing actions | AI Governance Lead + VP Crew Operations | High | Model-risk tier approval and HITL workflow not yet signed |
| Stale or ungoverned data drives confidently wrong recovery decision | Owner-signed freshness SLA and lineage on crew legality, PNR, flight status, operational event store | VP Data Platforms | High | Certified freshness SLA and actual freshness not yet loaded |
| No override log or accountable control owner per AI initiative | Override capture, decision audit trail, named control owner per initiative | AI Governance Lead | High | Control owner + override log absent across 8 loaded AI initiatives |
| Board-grade value claims outrun Finance baseline | Finance-approved disruption-cost baseline by event category before value claims | CFO Office | Medium | No finance-approved realized-value row; benefits realization rows still Projected/Observed |
| Vendor/platform failure on OCC, Crew Recovery Optimizer, PSS gateway breaks autonomous path | Contract-to-system linkage, support SLA, resilience testing on IROPS-critical platforms | EVP Operations + CTO | Medium | Contract-system linkage and support SLA not yet tied to IROPS operating path |
| Adoption and realized-value evidence missing | Measured usage, decision latency, override rate, realized ops value per initiative | VP Digital Products | Medium | Adoption telemetry not yet instrumented across the 8 AI initiatives | The next useful move: pick two IROPS AI initiatives — I'd suggest the IROPS Decision Assistant and the Crew Recovery Copilot — and stand up the full control envelope (model-risk tier, HITL workflow, data-freshness signoff, override log, named control owner) on those two before extending autonomy anywhere else.
That gives the board a concrete, evidenced proof point rather than a portfolio-wide assertion. Want me to sequence the readiness gates into a roadmap, or pressure-test which two initiatives should carry the first control envelope?
